  **Key limitations:** Formal source entries for the baptism (src_002) and marriage (src_001) are both logged as derivative; the original register image was confirmed by transcription but is not registered as a separate source entry, preventing a formal "proved" assessment. The name form "Janna" vs. "Jantje" requires a well-supported but inferential step. No unsearched reachable records remain.
  
  **Next step:** All questions resolved. Project is complete.
  
  ---
  
  Jantje Willems, the wife of Jacob Jeltes in 18th-century Groningen, was in all likelihood baptized on 23 May 1751 at the Dutch Reformed church in the city of Groningen, and her parents were Willem Jans and Trijntje Harmens. This rests on a handwritten church baptism register entry — confirmed from the original image — that names both parents directly at the time of the event. The name used at her baptism was "Janna," a different but equivalent Dutch form of the same name as "Jantje," the form that appears in her 1772 marriage record; both are recognized diminutives of the formal name Johanna in this region and period. Two independent threads corroborate the identification: Jantje's first daughter, born in 1774, was named Trijntje — exactly as Dutch custom required for a child named after the maternal grandmother — and Jantje's own surname "Willems" means "daughter of Willem," which matches the father's name in the baptism record. A second family with a father named Willem and a mother whose name also began with Trijntje was thoroughly searched and found to have no daughter named Jantje or Janna among their children, ruling them out. The one gap is that the research records describe the baptism index rather than the original register as the formal source, and the name equivalence requires a step of interpretation — two reasons why this is a likely rather than a definitive conclusion. Every place this information was likely to have been recorded was searched.
  
  This research is finished. If you'd like a second opinion on it, just ask.
